claim: fetch request streams cannot measure upload progress because they measure when data leaves your stream, not when it is delivered; XHR remains the way to get upload progress today.
quote: you end up measuring the point at which the data is taken from your stream ... If you want progress events today, the best way is to use XHR

claim: Streaming request bodies in fetch require duplex: 'half' and HTTP/2+; the request must complete before the response is available.
quote: duplex: 'half' means that the request must complete before the response becomes available.

claim: beforeunload requires sticky activation, shows only a generic browser string, is triggered via preventDefault(), and disables bfcache in Firefox when a listener is attached.
quote: The browser will only show the dialog box if the frame or any embedded frame receives a user gesture or user interaction. ... Firefox will not place pages in the bfcache if they have beforeunload listeners, and this is bad for performance.

claim: React Router 7 useBlocker blocks client-side navigation with blocker.state idle|blocked and proceed()/reset(); available in Framework and Data mode only.
quote: let blocker = useBlocker(useCallback(() => isDirty, [isDirty]));

claim: React Router ships useBeforeUnload as a thin wrapper over window.onbeforeunload, intended for persisting state before the user leaves.
quote: This hook is just a helper around window.onbeforeunload. It can be useful to save important application state on the page (to something like the browser's local storage), before the user navigates away from your page.

claim: TanStack Router's useBlocker/Block covers router navigation via shouldBlockFn and browser hard navigation via an enableBeforeUnload option that registers the beforeunload handler.
quote: For page events that we cannot control directly, we rely on the browser's onbeforeunload event.

claim: Next.js added the onNavigate prop to <Link> in v15.3.0; it exposes preventDefault() but only fires on same-origin client-side navigations from that Link.
quote: An event handler called during client-side navigation. The handler receives an event object that includes a preventDefault() method, allowing you to cancel the navigation if needed. ... External URLs won't trigger onNavigate since it's only for client-side and same-origin navigations.

claim: Server Action request bodies are capped at 1MB by default, configurable via serverActions.bodySizeLimit; the limit applies to the raw multipart body including boundary overhead.
quote: By default, the maximum size of the request body sent to a Server Action is 1MB ... The limit applies to the raw HTTP request body, including the bytes that multipart/form-data adds for boundaries, part headers, and field metadata.

claim: The request for a first-party navigation guard in the Next.js App Router (a replacement for Pages Router routeChangeStart) has been open since March 2023 with no substantive official answer.
quote: router events have been removed entirely

claim: next-navigation-guard is the de-facto community shim that intercepts router.push/back/forward in the App Router; last release 0.2.0 (Jun 2025).
quote: next-navigation-guard

claim: useOptimistic renders an optimistic value only while an Action is pending, converges with real state in the same render, and its setter must be called inside a Transition/Action.
quote: Optimistic state only renders while an Action is in progress, otherwise value is rendered. ... There's no extra render to "clear" the optimistic state.

claim: TanStack Form implements autosave with form-level listeners: onChangeDebounceMs plus an onChange that calls formApi.handleSubmit() when the form is valid.
quote: onChange: ({ formApi, fieldApi }) => { if (formApi.state.isValid) { formApi.handleSubmit() } }

claim: React Hook Form's isDirty is a deep-equality comparison of current values against defaultValues; dirtyFields is tracked per field and is not kept in sync with isDirty.
quote: isDirty ... Make sure to provide all inputs' defaultValues at the useForm, so hook form can have a single source of truth to compare whether the form is dirty.

claim: isDirty going true while dirtyFields stays empty is a recurring, still-reported RHF behaviour, usually from setValue without shouldDirty or unstable defaultValues.
quote: form isDirty is true when dirtyFields is empty

claim: @uppy/aws-s3 (v5.2.1) handles both single-PUT and S3 multipart uploads; by default files <=100 MiB go in one chunk, larger ones multipart, and the plugin absorbed the deprecated @uppy/aws-s3-multipart.
quote: all files with a file.size <= 100 MiB will be uploaded in a single chunk, all files larger than that as multipart.

claim: Uppy's Golden Retriever restores selected files after a crash or refresh using LocalStorage for state, IndexedDB for files under ~5MiB, and an optional Service Worker for larger ones, with a 24h default expiry.
quote: first restores state from LocalStorage and then checks both file storages — IndexedDB and ServiceWorker — merging the results.

claim: react-dropzone is actively maintained: v15 (Feb 2026) changed isDragReject reset semantics, v16 and v17 (both 12 Jul 2026) dropped UMD, went ESM+CJS, rewrote the source in TypeScript and removed prop-types/defaultProps.
quote: Requires React >= 18. prop-types and defaultProps are removed in favor of TypeScript types and default parameter values

claim: 2026 comparison: react-dropzone ~3.5M weekly downloads / ~12KB / headless, no upload; FilePond ~700K / ~48KB / opinionated UI; @uppy/core ~500K / ~40KB modular with tus, S3 and cloud sources.
quote: react-dropzone | ~3.5M | ~12KB | Headless ... FilePond | ~700K | ~48KB | Opinionated UI ... @uppy/core | ~500K | ~40KB+ (modular)

claim: tus 1.0.0 has been frozen since 2016 and is explicitly declared stable for general adoption.
quote: Following SemVer, as of 1.0.0 tus is ready for general adoption. We don't expect to make breaking changes, but if we do, those will have to be in a 2.0.0.

claim: The IETF httpbis 'Resumable Uploads for HTTP' draft is at revision 11, Standards Track, still not an RFC as of mid-2026; it is intended to replace the core of tus v1.
quote: Resumable Uploads for HTTP — draft-ietf-httpbis-resumable-upload-11, Standards Track

claim: Cloudflare R2 supports presigned URLs for PUT/GET/HEAD but not multipart HTML form POST uploads; multipart state (uploadId, part ETags) must be brokered by your own Worker/API.
quote: multipart form uploads via HTML forms) is not currently supported

claim: Direct browser uploads to R2 require explicit bucket CORS rules or the browser blocks the PUT.
quote: CORS rules tell R2 which web domains are allowed to make requests

claim: workbox-background-sync queues failed requests in IndexedDB and replays them on a sync event, falling back to replay-on-service-worker-startup where the Background Sync API is missing.
quote: In browsers that don't natively support the BackgroundSync API, Workbox Background Sync will automatically attempt a replay whenever your service worker starts up.

claim: Background Sync API support is Chromium-only: ~77% global, zero support in Safari (all versions, including iOS) and Firefox.
quote: Safari Status: Completely unsupported across all versions (3.1 through TP), including Safari on iOS. Global Support: 77.48%

claim: Uppy 5.0 (1 Sep 2025) added headless components and hooks (useDropzone, useFileInput, useWebcam) behind an <UppyContextProvider />, and deprecated @uppy/status-bar, @uppy/informer and @uppy/progress-bar.
quote: Uppy 5.0 introduces composable UI components and hooks that provide granular control without sacrificing first-class framework support.

claim: 2026 IndexedDB wrapper comparison: idb ~20M weekly downloads / ~3KB, localForage ~7.4M, Dexie ~1.5M / ~65KB; without navigator.storage.persist() browsers may evict IndexedDB under storage pressure.
quote: the browser may evict IndexedDB data under storage pressure ... navigator.storage.persist(), which asks the browser to not evict your data.

claim: react-dropzone latest is 17.0.0, published 2026-07-12.
The standard optimistic-concurrency pattern is to send the ETag you read back as If-Match; a stale ETag yields HTTP 412 Precondition Failed instead of a silent overwrite.
quote: if the blob's current ETag value differs from the ETag value specified in the If-Match header, Azure Storage returns HTTP status code 412 (Precondition Failed).

claim: Client-supplied Content-Type and file extension are attacker-controlled; magic-byte sniffing is stronger but still spoofable, so server-side revalidation is mandatory.
quote: Applications that rely solely on the Content-Type header sent by clients can be bypassed by attackers who manipulate this header

claim: Large multipart FormData sent to a Next.js 15 Server Action can drop binary data on the request body — a reported failure mode for routing real uploads through Server Actions.
quote: Next15 - Large file upload with FormData drops binary data on request body

claim: The recommended shape for React 19 uploads is to upload the bytes direct-to-storage from the browser and pass only the resulting URL/key to the Server Action, because Server Actions give no progress and no resumability.
quote: Uploading files through a server action works fine for small, simple cases. But once you need things like large file support, resumable uploads, image transformations, or CDN delivery, building that yourself is a significant chunk of infrastructure work.

claim: Dexie is the IndexedDB wrapper positioned for offline-first apps, with useLiveQuery giving React components reactive reads from the local store.
quote: Build Offline-First Apps with IndexedDB Made Simple

claim: react-admin's <AutoSave> is production prior art: 3000ms debounce after the last change, requires keepDirtyValues, and cannot be combined with warnWhenUnsavedChanges because it implements its own guard.
quote: will save the current form values 3 seconds after the last change ... You can't use <Form warnWhenUnsavedChanges> with this component. <AutoSave> implements its own similar mechanism, and it's enabled by default.

claim: The common draft-autosave recipe is debounce the dirty form state, persist to storage, and surface an explicit saving/saved/error status indicator.
quote: Auto-save forms detect changes, debounce the save trigger, and provide clear visual feedback about save status.

claim: react-dropzone is a hooks-first drag-and-drop zone (useDropzone) that hands you File objects and deliberately does not perform the upload.
quote: Simple React hook to create a HTML5-compliant drag'n'drop zone for files.

claim: R2 multipart uploads are created, parted and completed as discrete S3-compatible operations, which is what a browser client must drive when each part is individually presigned.
quote: you can expose an HTTP API that a client application can call to create, upload parts for, and complete a multipart upload
